f1.quote: Mo content in CoCrFeNiMox-Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 composites was varied from x = 0.2 to 0.5 and 1

f2.quote: Spark plasma sintering was performed under vacuum and 40 MPa by heating to 1250 °C at 150 °C/min, holding for 3 min, and furnace cooling.

f3.quote: Ball-on-disk tests were conducted in air at room temperature, 200, 400, 600, and 800 °C against a 6 mm Si3N4 ball, using an 8 N load, 4 mm rotation radius, 0.15 m/s sliding speed, and 270 m sliding distance.

f4.quote: Increasing Mo produced Mo-induced FCC lattice distortion and increasing amounts of a hard, Mo-rich tetragonal σ phase

f5.quote: Dissolved Mo impedes dislocation motion through solid-solution strengthening, and the hard σ phase suppresses plastic deformation and scratching through second-phase strengthening.

f6.quote: At lower temperatures, layered MoS2 supplies a low-shear film and soft Ag reduces adhesion

f7.quote: Mo1 developed a particularly continuous, dense glaze at 800 °C containing NiO and Ag2MoO4, Ag2Mo4O13, and Ag2Mo2O7.

f8.quote: increasing Mo was predicted to increase hardness
